card.intuition: Parameters are the numbers inside a model — often billions — tuned during training and frozen afterward. Everything a model 'knows' lives in them, and inference uses them unchanged. Nothing you do in a session changes them; only more training produces new parameters and thus a different model.
card.analogy: Parameters are like a compiled binary's machine code: the compiler (training) wrote them once, every run just executes them, and a runtime patch does nothing — you need a new build.
card.time_complexity: Inference cost scales with parameter count — a trillion-parameter model multiplies every input token through far more weights than a small one, which is why bigger tiers are slower and pricier per request.
card.space_complexity: Parameter memory is fixed and lives on the provider's hardware; nothing in the context window changes it, so your whole session budget goes to the tokens the harness assembles, never to the weights.
when_to_use: Deciding between fine-tuning and loading material into context — retraining yields a different model
Explaining why a model's built-in knowledge stops at its knowledge cutoff
Accounting for tier cost differences driven by parameter count
Diagnosing a behavior change as parameters versus harness or context
gotchas: No correction or codebase you show in a session changes the parameters — the model stays stateless
Fine-tuning updates the parameters and produces a different model, usually far costlier than context for one project
